title: Strict Equilibrium Is Proper
body_html:
Strict Equilibrium Is Proper

Every strict equilibrium of a finite normal-form game is a proper equilibrium.
proof_html:
Sketch

If $s$ is strict, then for small perturbations of the opponents, each $s_i$ remains the unique best response of player $i$. Using proper equilibria of the restricted game where each player is prevented from playing $s_i$, the profiles $\sigma^\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)s+\epsilon\tau^\epsilon$ are $\epsilon$-proper and converge to $s$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Rem. 6.5.8] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Every strict equilibrium is proper.
